newsitem.title: USA: Network Long Distance pursues acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Network Long Distance pursues acquisitions.

text.p: Network Long Distance Inc, which on Tuesday finalized its acquisition of United WATS Inc, plans to keep making acquisitions as it shoots for its target of $100 million in annual revenues.

"I am extremely confident in our ability to reach $100 million...both through renewed internal sale efforts as well as... acquisitions," said Louis Resweber, president and chief executive of the company's merger and acquisition subsidiary.
Reswebber told a conference call the company has about 25 candidates in the acquisition pool that shortly will be whittled down to two or three.
Shares of the Baton Rouge-based company were up 1/8 to 9-1/8 at midafternoon on Tuesday.
Network Long Distance announced in September it would merge with United WATS, an inter-exchange carrier for businesses which has about $21 million in revenues.
Resweber said the United WATS buy has helped the company boost its annualized revenues to $60 million.
He also said the acquisition would result in a one-time charge causing a loss in its December third quarter but the company expected to return to profitability as early as January 1997.

"You can anticipate a charge from merger expenses in the December-ended quarter," he said, without divulging the amount. After the writedown, "you can see us move back into an area of profitability," he said.

"We're really only two UWI's (United WATS Inc's) away from hitting the $100 million mark," he said. "It would not be a preposterous thought to think of us doing at least one if not two more deals the size of UWI."
United WATS will help Network Long Distance grow through new sales and acquisitions, particularly because of United's longstanding relationship with Sprint Corp and MCI Communications Corp, he said.
"We can introduce our products now as well as the products of two of the best known brand names in the industry -- Sprint and MCI -- to our customer base," Resweber said.
"For the first time, we have opened ourselves up to target acquisition candidates with a Sprint and MCI base in that now there will be some economies of scale," he said.
Network Long Distance last weeek posted a second-quarter loss of $0.04 per share on revenues of $10.2 million compared with a profit of $0.03 per share last year on revenues of $7.8 million.
